questions.question: Which of the following is not protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. This includes sturdy jackets and pants that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: The single most effective thing you can do to survive an accident is:

options.text: Ask others about how to ride more safely.

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most important thing you can do to reduce your risk of injury or death in an accident.

questions.question: Which of the following does not need to be checked regularly?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle's tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes before every ride. Small mechanical problems can be very dangerous.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface for motorcycles?
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road. Ride with extra caution on these surfaces.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe since there is so much traffic there.

questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because many cars and motorcycles cross paths there, creating conflicts.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Slow down when riding on a slippery surface. Sudden moves can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid slippery roads.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Inspect your motorcycle before every ride. This takes a few minutes and helps prevent problems before you enter traffic.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
Only have one set of footrests.
Not encourage the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other motorists that a passenger is on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat for two riders and footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear that you do.

questions.question: The best way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let a tailgater pass when possible. Speeding up may cause the driver to tailgate at higher speeds, which increases danger.

questions.question: Combining alcohol and over-the-counter drugs:

options.text: Causes the side effects of both substances to cancel out.
Will not affect your riding abilities.

questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can affect your ability to ride safely. Some drugs become more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should wear a jacket:

options.text: At all times, no matter the weather.
Only if you will ride for longer than 30 minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, no matter the weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding a motorcycle. It protects you from injury and helps prevent sunburn and dehydration, even in hot weather.

questions.question: On which surface does a motorcycle have the best grip?
questions.explanation: Dry pavement gives the best traction. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, and metal plates are all hazardous for motorcycles.

questions.question: Which sign is typically rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must obey the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The more alcohol builds up in your body.
The faster your body removes it.
The less the alcohol affects you.
The better your chances of avoiding a traffic stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The more alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the more alcohol builds up in your body. Never operate a motorcycle after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: If you drink just one alcoholic drink:

options.text: Your judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
It usually has no effect on your body.
It affects you, but only for a short time.
You can eliminate it by drinking coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your judgment and riding skills. Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol. Coffee cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour. If someone drank 8 drinks 4 hours ago, how much alcohol likely remains?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus 4 hours equals about 4 drinks remaining in the body.
